venue.name: Gonzales Hill Observatory (Walbran Park)
venue.description: Gonzales Hill Regional Park is a 1.80 hectare Capital Regional District park on Denison Road in Victoria/Oak Bay, established in 1992. The Capital Regional District, which owns and operates it, describes ocean views from the highest point (66 metres) on the south coast of Vancouver Island, rocky knolls to look out from, Garry oak trees and rare wildflowers in the meadows in spring. The Gonzales Observatory, on the hill, was a weather station for 75 years and is now described by the CRD as a historical landmark; the park page does not say the building is open to visitors. The park is open sunrise to sunset, lists hiking, walking/running and wildflowers as its activities with an easy difficulty rating, and lists a parking lot and public transit as its only amenities.
restrictions: Keep your dog under control or on a leash.
Stay on marked trails and do not disturb plants or animals.
Clean up after your dog and take all your trash with you.
Smoking is not allowed in parks or on trails.
Bicycles and motorized vehicles are not allowed.
Camping, open fires, and alcohol are not allowed.
venue.seasonal_notes: Visit in the spring to see wildflowers blooming in the Garry oak meadows.

programs.name: Self-guided park visit
programs.description: The CRD publishes no booked or guided program at this park; it is a drop-in regional park open sunrise to sunset. The park is 1.80 hectares with an easy difficulty rating, and the listed activities are hiking, walking/running and wildflowers. Amenities listed are a parking lot and public transit. Directions given are: from Victoria, follow Fairfield Road, which turns into Beach Drive in Oak Bay Municipality, turn right on Denison Road, which leads to the park entrance on the right, roughly 10 minutes' driving time from downtown Victoria. By bus, BC Transit route 7 to Fairfield Road at Foul Bay Road leaves an approximately 1.5 kilometre walk to the park. A park map is published as a PDF. The CRD's Regional Parks Interpretive School Programs are delivered at Island View Beach, Elk/Beaver Lake, Francis/King and Witty's Lagoon; Gonzales Hill is not among them.
programs.what_children_do: Walk up easy marked trails from the Denison Road parking lot to the rocky knolls, look out over the ocean and the city, look at the white domed observatory from outside, and in spring find wildflowers in the Garry oak meadows.
programs.our_note: It is a very small park - under two hectares - so it is a half-hour stop rather than a morning, and the payoff is the view. The observatory is described only as a historical landmark, with nothing on the page about going inside, so check before you promise a group they will see it. Nothing is listed here but a parking lot: no washrooms, no picnic tables, no shelter.
programs.practical_summary: A parking lot and a bus stop about 1.5 km away are the only access facilities listed; no washrooms, picnic area or rain shelter appear in the CRD's amenities for this park. There is nothing to book, and no cost is published either way.

images.alt: A white observatory with a big dome on a rocky hill.

gaps: The website listed in the tracker, www.tourismvictoria.com, is a third-party tourism board and was not used. The park is owned and operated by the Capital Regional District, and the CRD's own park page is recorded as the website.

The CRD page covers Gonzales Hill Regional Park. Walbran Park, the adjoining green space that locals also call Gonzales Hill, is a District of Oak Bay park and is not described on the CRD page; nothing about it has been extracted here.
The observatory building itself: the CRD page calls it a historical landmark and says nothing about public access, opening hours or interpretation inside. Whether a group can go in is unknown.
No cost is stated. The CRD page neither says the park is free nor lists a parking fee, so is_free is left null.

No washrooms, picnic tables, picnic shelter or drinking water are listed under Amenities - only a parking lot and public transit. Their absence from the list is not the same as the CRD stating there are none, so the facility fields are left null rather than false.

No group program, guided walk or booking route exists for this park on the CRD site. The CRD's Regional Parks Interpretive School Programs page (opened) names only Island View Beach, Elk/Beaver Lake, Francis/King and Witty's Lagoon as locations; Gonzales Hill is not mentioned.

No park-specific phone or email is published on the page beyond the CRD Regional Parks contact block (250.478.3344, crdparks@crd.bc.ca), which is a general enquiry and report-an-issue route, not a booking route.
Bus parking is not addressed. The page lists a parking lot without saying how large it is or whether a coach can use it.
Trail surface, gradient and wheelchair or stroller access at this park are not stated; the only accessibility signal is the general "Difficulty Rating: Easy".

No coordinates are published in a usable form. A Google Maps directions link on the page carries sll=48.41432,-123.323497 and ll=48.4161,-123.316941, but those are map viewport parameters rather than a published venue coordinate, so they were not used; the address was extracted and left for geocoding (geo_source geocode_pending).
The hero photograph is served from cdn.intelligencebank.com, the digital asset service the CRD's own site serves park photos from, and carries the CRD's own alt text.
